title: A Message Exchange About an Unexpected Flood
script: Nabila: [worried] Tomo, are you okay? I just saw on the news that the river near your street overflowed last night.
Tomo: [tired] We're fine, though the ground floor took in about knee-deep water before we managed to move everything upstairs in time.
Nabila: [relieved] Thank goodness you're safe. Did you get any warning beforehand, or did it just happen suddenly overnight?
Tomo: [explaining] There was a warning, actually, though it came only two hours before the water rose, which wasn't nearly enough time honestly.
Nabila: [concerned] Two hours seems dangerously short, given how much rain fell upstream over the past few days according to the reports.
Tomo: [frustrated] Exactly what several of us have been saying for years, yet nothing changed until it actually happened to us directly.
Nabila: [thoughtful] Do you think the new drainage construction upstream contributed to this, or was it simply an unusually heavy storm season?
Tomo: [honestly] Probably both, if I'm being fair. The storm was severe, but the drainage changes likely made the water rise faster than it would have otherwise.
Nabila: [gently] Even though this happened, I'm glad you got everyone out safely, despite how little warning time you actually had.
Tomo: [grateful] Me too. My elderly neighbor couldn't manage the stairs alone, so my brother carried her up, which honestly felt heroic in the moment.
Nabila: [curious] What are you doing now that the water has mostly receded from your street?
Tomo: [weary] Cleaning mud out of everything, throwing away ruined furniture, and trying to dry the walls before mold becomes an even bigger problem.
Nabila: [offering] I can come this weekend and help with the cleanup, if that would actually be useful rather than just one more person in your way.
Tomo: [warmly] It would genuinely help. Even in spite of everything lost, having extra hands makes this feel slightly less overwhelming.
Nabila: [determined] Then I'll bring gloves and old towels. Despite the damage, at least you and your family are safe, and that matters most.
Tomo: [sincerely] Thank you, Nabila. Honestly, moments like this remind me how much community matters when nature reminds us who's really in charge.
